final_message:
I reproduced the bug on 9.28.0 (f341f21). On the report's exact snippet, `++i` and `--i` are flagged and `i + 1` / `i - 1` are not.

`node bin/eslint.js --no-config-lookup --no-ignore repro/report.js`:
```
4:22  error  This assigned value is not used in subsequent statements  no-useless-assignment
5:22  error  This assigned value is not used in subsequent statements  no-useless-assignment
```

`node repro/repro-19818.js` runs a larger set of cases through `Linter` and exits 1. Seven cases are flagged where the assigned value is clearly used:

| Code | Reported? |
|---|---|
| `[1,2,3].map(i => ++i)` | yes |
| `[1,2,3].map(i => --i)` | yes |
| `function f(i) { return ++i; }` | yes |
| `function f() { let x = 0; return ++x; }` | yes |
| `function f() { let x = 0; console.log(++x); }` | yes |
| `function f(i) { return i += 1; }` | yes |
| `[1,2,3].map(i => (i = i + 1))` | yes |
| `i => i + 1`, `i => i - 1` | no |
| `i => i++` | yes (control: the new value really is never read, so this one looks correct) |

So the bug is wider than the report says. It isn't specific to `++`/`--` or to arrow functions: any assignment or update expression whose result is consumed by its parent (a return, an arrow body, a call argument) gets flagged when the variable isn't read again later.

**Likely cause (from reading the code; I haven't debugged it):** in `lib/rules/no-useless-assignment.js`, the `":matches(VariableDeclarator[init!=null], AssignmentExpression, UpdateExpression):exit"` handler records the assignment. `verifyAssignmentIsUsed` then only counts the variable as used if one of its read references is evaluated after the assignment, in the same segment or a later one. Nothing checks whether the parent node uses the expression's own value. For `++i`, the only read reference is the same `i` identifier being written, so it's never counted as a later read. The existing tests in `tests/lib/rules/no-useless-assignment.js` only cover `++`/`--` as standalone statements, so this path is untested.

The patch adds only `repro/report.js` and `repro/repro-19818.js`. No rule code is changed.
